e2f19f15-d745-424f-87cf-59575ba62e07.text:
Which of the following best describes 'barzakh' in Islam?
A) Paradise
B) A state of waiting between death and the Day of Judgement
C) Hell
D) Reincarnation
e2f19f15-d745-424f-87cf-59575ba62e07.marks: B — A state of waiting between death and the Day of Judgement [1 mark]

e2f19f15-d745-424f-87cf-59575ba62e07.text: Give one Christian belief about what happens after death.
e2f19f15-d745-424f-87cf-59575ba62e07.marks:
1 mark for any one valid belief:
• Christians believe in heaven – a state of eternal happiness with God
• Christians believe in hell – eternal separation from God
• Some Christians (e.g. Catholics) believe in purgatory – where souls are purified before entering heaven
• Some Christians believe in the immortality of the soul
• Some Christians believe in the resurrection of the body at the end of time

e2f19f15-d745-424f-87cf-59575ba62e07.text: Explain two different beliefs about life after death. In your answer you should refer to Christianity and Islam.
e2f19f15-d745-424f-87cf-59575ba62e07.marks:
Award up to 2 marks per belief explained (1 mark for a simple point, 2 for a developed point). If beliefs are not contrasting, maximum 2 marks.
• Some Christians believe in the immortality of the soul – that the soul continues living immediately after death, as shown by Jesus telling the thief on the cross he would be in paradise that day (Luke 23:43) (2)
• Muslims believe that after death the soul enters barzakh, a state of waiting, and will not enter Jannah or Jahannam until the Day of Judgement when all people are resurrected and judged by Allah (2)
Alternatively: Christians may believe in purgatory (Catholic view) vs Muslims who do not have a concept of purgatory – in Islam the soul waits in barzakh instead.

e2f19f15-d745-424f-87cf-59575ba62e07.text: Explain two religious beliefs about how belief in an afterlife affects the value of human life. Refer to scripture or sacred writings in your answer.
e2f19f15-d745-424f-87cf-59575ba62e07.marks:
Marking: First belief (1–2 marks) + Second belief (1–2 marks) + Source of authority named and applied (1–2 marks) = up to 6 marks.

Award 1 mark per simple point, 2 marks per developed point (maximum 4), plus 1 mark for a relevant reference to scripture or sacred writing.
• Christians believe life is valuable because it is given by God and is sacred. Belief in heaven motivates Christians to live according to God’s will so they can be rewarded with eternal life (2)
• Muslims believe life is a test from Allah. How they live determines whether they enter Jannah or Jahannam, so they are motivated to follow the Five Pillars and treat others with compassion (2)
• Scripture: “Truly I tell you, today you will be with me in Paradise” (Luke 23:43) – shows Christians that the afterlife begins after death, making earthly life a preparation for eternity (1)
OR: “No soul may die except with God’s permission at a predestined time” (Qur’an 3:145) – shows Muslims that God controls life and death (1)

e2f19f15-d745-424f-87cf-59575ba62e07.text:
'There must be life after death.' Evaluate this statement. In your answer you should:
• refer to Christian and/or Muslim teachings
• give reasoned arguments to support this statement
• give reasoned arguments to support a different point of view
• reach a justified conclusion.
e2f19f15-d745-424f-87cf-59575ba62e07.marks:
Lower band (1-3): One argument with justification.
Lower-mid band (4-6): Different arguments for and against with justification, OR several linked justified arguments for one position.
Upper-mid band (7-9): Good well-justified arguments for and against, linked together.
Top band (10-12): Very well argued. Well-justified arguments for and against, linked together and leading to a reasonable conclusion.
Points for:
• Jesus tells the thief on the cross that he will be in paradise – this implies heaven exists and life continues after death.
• Churches such as the Catholic Church teach that people go to heaven, hell, or purgatory after death.
• Muslims believe in akhirah as one of the six articles of faith – the Qur’an describes Jannah and Jahannam in detail.
• Belief in an afterlife gives life purpose and motivates moral behaviour.
Points against:
• Many Bible verses support resurrection at the end of time rather than immediate afterlife – there is disagreement even within Christianity.
• Many Christians do not believe in purgatory – it is not mentioned by Jesus directly.
• Non-religious people argue there is no scientific evidence for an afterlife.
• People from other religions (e.g. Hindus) believe in reincarnation, not heaven/hell – there is no agreement on what the afterlife looks like.

e2f19f15-d745-424f-87cf-59575ba62e07.text: Explain two Muslim beliefs about what happens after death. Refer to scripture or sacred writings in your answer.
e2f19f15-d745-424f-87cf-59575ba62e07.marks:
Marking: First belief (1–2 marks) + Second belief (1–2 marks) + Source of authority named and applied (1–2 marks) = up to 6 marks.

Award 1 mark per simple point, 2 marks per developed point (maximum 4), plus 1 mark for a relevant reference to scripture or sacred writing.
• Muslims believe that after death the soul enters barzakh – a state of waiting between death and the Day of Judgement where angels question the soul about its faith (2)
• On the Day of Judgement, all people will be resurrected and judged by Allah. Those who lived righteously will enter Jannah (paradise) and those who did evil will be sent to Jahannam (hell) (2)
• Scripture: “No soul may die except with God’s permission at a predestined time” (Qur’an 3:145) – shows that Allah controls life and death and has a plan for every person (1)
OR: “Do not kill each other, for God is merciful to you” (Qur’an 4:29) – reinforces the sanctity of life because Allah alone decides when life ends (1)

f4dccd5a-e797-4d94-9f76-cb70a6e2d596.text:
Which of the following best describes God as omnipotent?
A) God is all-loving
B) God is all-powerful
C) God is all-knowing
D) God is everywhere
f4dccd5a-e797-4d94-9f76-cb70a6e2d596.marks: The correct answer is B. Omnipotent means all-powerful — God has unlimited authority and power. [1 mark]

f4dccd5a-e797-4d94-9f76-cb70a6e2d596.text: Name one of the three persons of the Trinity.
f4dccd5a-e797-4d94-9f76-cb70a6e2d596.marks: Any one from: the Father / the Son / the Holy Spirit. [1 mark]

f4dccd5a-e797-4d94-9f76-cb70a6e2d596.text: Explain two ways in which belief in God as loving (benevolent) influences Christians today.
f4dccd5a-e797-4d94-9f76-cb70a6e2d596.marks:
Students may include:
• Christians feel valued and loved by God, which gives them confidence and self-worth. They believe God cares about them individually, which brings comfort in difficult times.
• Christians are motivated to share God’s love with others through practical acts of kindness, charity work and forgiveness — imitating the unconditional love God shows them.
• Because God is all-loving, Christians believe in forgiveness. This influences them to forgive others who wrong them, just as God forgives those who repent.
• John 3:16 teaches that God loved the world enough to send Jesus. This influences Christians to make sacrifices for others.
Two clear, developed points needed for full marks. [4 marks]

f4dccd5a-e797-4d94-9f76-cb70a6e2d596.text: Explain two Christian beliefs about the nature of God. Refer to sacred writings or another source of Christian belief and teaching in your answer.
f4dccd5a-e797-4d94-9f76-cb70a6e2d596.marks:
Students may include:
• God is omnipotent — all-powerful. Supported by Luke 1:37: ‘Nothing is impossible with God.’ This was spoken by the Angel Gabriel to Mary, showing God’s power has no limits. (1–2 marks)
• God is benevolent — all-loving. Supported by John 3:16: ‘God so loved the world that he gave his one and only Son.’ Sending Jesus is seen as God’s greatest act of love. (1–2 marks)
• God is just — fair. Supported by 2 Thessalonians 1:6: ‘God is just: He will pay back trouble to those who trouble you.’ (1–2 marks)
• Source named and applied to the belief for additional marks.
Two beliefs, each explained and supported by a source of authority. [6 marks]

f4dccd5a-e797-4d94-9f76-cb70a6e2d596.text:
‘The problem of evil and suffering proves that God does not exist.’
Evaluate this statement considering arguments for and against. In your response you should:
• refer to Christian teachings
• reach a justified conclusion.
f4dccd5a-e797-4d94-9f76-cb70a6e2d596.marks:
Arguments supporting the statement:
• If God is all-powerful and all-loving, he would want to and be able to stop suffering — yet suffering exists.
• The inconsistent triad, an argument pressed by David Hume: God cannot be omnipotent, benevolent and allow evil to exist at the same time.
• Natural evil (earthquakes, disease) cannot be blamed on human free will, making it harder to explain.
Arguments against the statement:
• Moral evil is explained by free will — God gave humans genuine choice, and some misuse it. This is not God’s fault.
• Suffering may be a test of faith. The story of Job shows God rewards those who remain faithful through suffering.
• God’s plan is beyond human understanding — ‘Before I formed you in the womb I knew you’ (Jeremiah 1:5).
• Belief in God brings hope and comfort through suffering, especially the promise of eternal life.
Top band (10-12): both sides argued in depth, religious teaching used throughout, and a conclusion that follows from the reasoning.
Upper-mid band (7-9): both sides given with reasons and clear religious content.
Mid band (4-6): one side argued with reasons, or both sides stated without development. An answer with no religious content stays in this band at best.
Low band (1-3): an opinion with a reason.
[12 marks]

f4dccd5a-e797-4d94-9f76-cb70a6e2d596.text: Explain two ways in which the belief in the Trinity influences Christians today.
f4dccd5a-e797-4d94-9f76-cb70a6e2d596.marks:
Students may include:
• Christians are baptised ‘in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit’ (Matthew 28:19). This shows the Trinity is central to how Christians enter the faith and shapes their worship practices.
• Belief in the Holy Spirit gives Christians confidence that God is active in the world today — guiding, comforting and strengthening them in daily life and decision-making.
• The Trinity helps Christians understand God’s relationship with humanity: the Father as creator, the Son as saviour, and the Spirit as ongoing guide.
• Christians recite the Nicene Creed which affirms the Trinity, uniting believers across different denominations in a shared statement of faith.
Two clear, developed points needed for full marks. [4 marks]

34dffb48-5974-48f2-b400-0bc21de2e5e9.text:
Which one of the following is a type of weapon of mass destruction?
A) Machine gun
B) Chemical weapon
C) Landmine
D) Drone
34dffb48-5974-48f2-b400-0bc21de2e5e9.marks: Answer: B) Chemical weapon. The three types of WMD are nuclear, biological, and chemical weapons. Machine guns, landmines, and drones are conventional weapons, not WMD.

34dffb48-5974-48f2-b400-0bc21de2e5e9.text: Give one reason why some religious believers oppose weapons of mass destruction.
34dffb48-5974-48f2-b400-0bc21de2e5e9.marks:
1 mark for one valid reason, such as:
• WMD kill innocent civilians, which goes against the sanctity of life.
• They cause indiscriminate destruction that cannot be limited to military targets.
• They harm the environment and future generations through radioactive fallout.
• They do not fulfil just war criteria.
• The money spent on WMD could be used to help the poor.

34dffb48-5974-48f2-b400-0bc21de2e5e9.text: Explain two different beliefs in contemporary British society about weapons of mass destruction. In your answer you should refer to the main religious tradition of Great Britain and one or more other religious traditions.
34dffb48-5974-48f2-b400-0bc21de2e5e9.marks:
First contrasting belief: simple explanation = 1 mark, detailed explanation = 2 marks. Second contrasting belief: simple explanation = 1 mark, detailed explanation = 2 marks.
Students may include:
• Some Christians, such as Quakers, are pacifists and oppose all WMD because Jesus taught peace and loving your enemies. The Christian Campaign for Nuclear Disarmament calls for the permanent elimination of nuclear weapons.
• Some Muslims believe WMD are not approved by Allah because they go beyond self-defence and kill indiscriminately, contradicting the Qur'an's teaching that responses to attack must be proportionate.
• Some Christians accept nuclear deterrence as a way to maintain peace and prevent attack, arguing it saves more lives in the long run.
Students must refer to Christianity and at least one other tradition.

34dffb48-5974-48f2-b400-0bc21de2e5e9.text: Explain two religious beliefs about nuclear weapons. Refer to scripture or sacred writings in your answer.
34dffb48-5974-48f2-b400-0bc21de2e5e9.marks:
Marking: First belief (1–2 marks) + Second belief (1–2 marks) + Source of authority named and applied (1–2 marks) = up to 6 marks.

First belief: simple explanation = 1 mark, detailed explanation = 2 marks. Second belief: simple explanation = 1 mark, detailed explanation = 2 marks. Relevant scripture reference = 1 mark.
Students may include:
• Many Christians oppose nuclear weapons because they cause indiscriminate destruction. Jesus taught 'Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of God' (Matthew 5:9), meaning Christians should promote peace rather than stockpile weapons that could kill millions.
• Many Muslims believe nuclear weapons are not approved by Allah because the Qur'an teaches that responses to aggression must be proportionate: 'If you have to respond to an attack, make your response proportionate' (Qur'an 16:126). Nuclear weapons cause disproportionate, indiscriminate destruction.
• Some Christians may accept nuclear deterrence to protect innocent lives, applying the principle of 'love your neighbour' (Matthew 22:39) by keeping peace through strength.

34dffb48-5974-48f2-b400-0bc21de2e5e9.text:
'Weapons of mass destruction should be banned.' Evaluate this statement. In your answer you:
• should give reasoned arguments in support of this statement
• should give reasoned arguments to support a different point of view
• should refer to religious arguments
• may refer to non-religious arguments
• should reach a justified conclusion.
34dffb48-5974-48f2-b400-0bc21de2e5e9.marks:
Arguments in support:
• WMD kill indiscriminately, including innocent civilians, which goes against the sanctity of life taught by both Christianity and Islam.
• Jesus taught 'Blessed are the peacemakers' (Matthew 5:9) — possessing WMD is the opposite of peacemaking.
• The Prophet Muhammad forbade the killing of innocent civilians — WMD cannot distinguish between combatants and civilians.
• Several popes have spoken out against WMD because of the harm to people, the environment, and the waste of money that could help the poor.
• WMD do not fulfil just war criteria as they cause disproportionate harm.
Arguments against:
• Nuclear deterrence has arguably prevented major wars since 1945 — the fear of mutually assured destruction keeps nations from attacking.
• Some Christians and Muslims accept that weapons may be kept for self-defence without intending to use them.
• The Qur'an states 'Those who have been attacked are permitted to take up arms' (Qur'an 22:39) — some interpret this as permitting powerful defensive weapons.
• Utilitarians may argue that keeping WMD prevents greater suffering overall.
• Unilateral disarmament could leave a country vulnerable to attack.
Conclusion should be justified and follow logically from the arguments presented.
Top band (10-12): A well-argued response with developed reasoning, religious and non-religious arguments on both sides, and a justified conclusion.
Upper-mid band (7-9): Some developed arguments with religious references.
Lower-mid band (4-6): Basic reasoning with some relevant points.
Low band (1-3): Simple, undeveloped points.
spelling/grammar: up to 3 additional marks.

34dffb48-5974-48f2-b400-0bc21de2e5e9.text: Explain two religious teachings about weapons of mass destruction. Refer to scripture or sacred writings in your answer.
34dffb48-5974-48f2-b400-0bc21de2e5e9.marks:
Marking: First belief (1–2 marks) + Second belief (1–2 marks) + Source of authority named and applied (1–2 marks) = up to 6 marks.

First teaching: simple explanation = 1 mark, detailed explanation = 2 marks. Second teaching: simple explanation = 1 mark, detailed explanation = 2 marks. Relevant scripture reference = 1 mark.
Students may include:
• Christians believe WMD contradict the teaching to 'love your neighbour as yourself' (Matthew 22:39) because they cause indiscriminate suffering to innocent people. Several popes have spoken out against WMD, arguing the money spent could help the poor instead.
• Muslims believe WMD go beyond what is permitted in self-defence. The Qur'an teaches that violence must be proportionate: 'If you have to respond to an attack, make your response proportionate' (Qur'an 16:126). WMD cause disproportionate destruction and harm civilians, which Muhammad explicitly forbade.

20e03b77-d479-413a-a29f-148bcad6f4ed.text:
Which one of the following is the name given to the practice in some religions of having more than one wife?
A) Procreation
B) Contraception
C) Stability
D) Polygamy
Give one religious belief about the purpose of families.
20e03b77-d479-413a-a29f-148bcad6f4ed.marks:
1 mark for one simple point.
Possible answers:
• To fulfil God’s command to procreate (have children)
• To raise and educate children in a faith
• To provide stability, love and security for family members
• To protect children from harm
• To reflect the family of God (Christian)
• To provide a basis for a stable society

20e03b77-d479-413a-a29f-148bcad6f4ed.text:
Explain two different beliefs in contemporary British society about same-sex parents.
In your answer you should refer to the main religious tradition of Great Britain and one or more other religious traditions.
20e03b77-d479-413a-a29f-148bcad6f4ed.marks:
Award up to 4 marks, 2 per contrasting belief.
Possible answers:
• Some Christians say it is more important for children to be in a secure and loving family regardless of the gender of their parents. They believe love is the most important factor in raising children (2 marks).
• Muslims generally do not approve of same-sex parenting because Islam considers homosexuality morally wrong and believes children need both a male and female role model as parents (2 marks).
Alternatively: Some traditional Christians also oppose same-sex parenting because they believe children should grow up with a mother and father.

20e03b77-d479-413a-a29f-148bcad6f4ed.text:
Explain two religious beliefs about the role of parents in a family.
Refer to scripture or sacred writings in your answer.
20e03b77-d479-413a-a29f-148bcad6f4ed.marks:
Marking: First belief (1–2 marks) + Second belief (1–2 marks) + Source of authority named and applied (1–2 marks) = up to 6 marks.

Award up to 6 marks: 1 mark per simple point, 2 marks per developed point, 1 mark for a relevant reference to scripture. If only one religious belief is mentioned, maximum 2 marks + 1 mark for scriptural reference.
Possible answers:
• Christians believe parents must care for and provide for their families. ‘Anyone who does not provide for their relatives, and especially for their own household, has denied the faith and is worse than an unbeliever’ (1 Timothy 5:8). This shows that failing to look after your family goes against the Christian faith (developed point + scripture = 3 marks).
• Muslims believe parents should raise their children in the faith of Islam, teaching them to pray and live a good Muslim life. The Hadith teaches: ‘Honour your children and perfect their manners.’ This shows that parents have a duty to set a moral example (developed point + scripture = 3 marks).

20e03b77-d479-413a-a29f-148bcad6f4ed.text:
'Same-sex parents are just as good at bringing up children as other parents.'
Evaluate this statement.
In your answer you:
• should give reasoned arguments in support of this statement
• should give reasoned arguments to support a different point of view
• should refer to religious arguments
• may refer to non-religious arguments
• should reach a justified conclusion.
20e03b77-d479-413a-a29f-148bcad6f4ed.marks:
One argument with justification: 1–3 marks
Different arguments for and against, with justification: 4–6 marks OR Several linked, justified arguments for one position
Good, well-justified arguments for and against, linked together: 7–9 marks
Very well argued. Well-justified arguments for and against, linked together and leading to a reasonable conclusion: 10–12 marks

Points FOR:
• It is not loving to discriminate and not allow people to have children based on their sexuality.
• Same-sex couples adopting can give children without parents a good, loving home.
• Some Christians approve because they believe love is the most important factor, not the gender of the parents.
• Research shows children raised by same-sex parents develop just as well as other children.

Points AGAINST:
• Some traditional Christians believe children need a male and female role model. The Catholic Church teaches that heterosexual nuclear families are the foundation for a stable society.
• Muslims believe homosexuality is morally wrong, so same-sex parents cannot set a good moral example to their children according to Islamic teachings.
• The Bible implies marriage and family should be between a man and a woman: ‘God made them male and female’ (Mark 10:6).

Accept any relevant point or justification. Other religions should be accepted.

20e03b77-d479-413a-a29f-148bcad6f4ed.text:
Explain two religious beliefs about the nature of the family.
Refer to scripture or sacred writings in your answer.
20e03b77-d479-413a-a29f-148bcad6f4ed.marks:
Marking: First belief (1–2 marks) + Second belief (1–2 marks) + Source of authority named and applied (1–2 marks) = up to 6 marks.

Award up to 6 marks: 1 mark per simple point, 2 marks per developed point, 1 mark for a relevant reference to scripture. If only one religious belief is mentioned, maximum 2 marks + 1 mark for scriptural reference.
Possible answers:
• Christians believe the family provides the basis for a stable society and reflects the family of God. ‘Children are a heritage from the Lord, offspring a reward from him’ (Psalm 127:3). This shows that having a family is seen as a gift and blessing from God (developed point + scripture = 3 marks).
• In Islam, the extended family is the basis of Islamic society and part of God’s plan for human beings. The Qur’an teaches: ‘Your Lord has commanded that you should worship none but Him, and that you be kind to your parents’ (Qur’an 17:23). This shows the importance of family relationships in Islam (developed point + scripture = 3 marks).

05a8055c-6c6b-4a22-9e43-4ab0d3287db9.text:
Which one of the following best describes the 'sanctity of life'?
A) The belief that punishment should deter criminals
B) The belief that all life is holy and created by God
C) The belief that an action is right if it brings happiness to the majority
D) The belief that criminals deserve retribution
05a8055c-6c6b-4a22-9e43-4ab0d3287db9.marks: B — The belief that all life is holy and created by God [1 mark]

05a8055c-6c6b-4a22-9e43-4ab0d3287db9.text: Give one reason why people are against the death penalty.
05a8055c-6c6b-4a22-9e43-4ab0d3287db9.marks:
1 mark for one correct reason. Answers may include:
• Innocent people could be wrongly executed
• It does not allow for reformation
• It is inhumane and degrading
• It does not appear to deter criminals
• It contradicts the law on murder / makes the state a killer
• It goes against the sanctity of life
[1 mark]

05a8055c-6c6b-4a22-9e43-4ab0d3287db9.text: Explain two different religious beliefs in contemporary British society about the use of the death penalty.
05a8055c-6c6b-4a22-9e43-4ab0d3287db9.marks:
Students may include some of the following points, but all other relevant points must be credited:
• Point 1 (Against): Most Christians believe only God has the right to take life. Jesus taught forgiveness, not retribution. He stopped a woman being put to death for adultery in John 8. The Ten Commandments state 'You shall not murder' (Exodus 20:13).
• Point 2 (For): Some Christians / Muslims may support it. The Old Testament teaches 'life for life, eye for eye' (Exodus 21). In Islam, Shari'ah law permits the death penalty for certain serious crimes as a hudud punishment. The Qur'an states 'Do not take life except by right.'

1 mark per simple point, 2 marks per developed point (maximum 4). If the two beliefs are not contrasting, maximum 2 marks.
[4 marks]

05a8055c-6c6b-4a22-9e43-4ab0d3287db9.text: Explain two religious beliefs about the use of the death penalty. Refer to sacred writings or another source of religious belief and teaching in your answer.
05a8055c-6c6b-4a22-9e43-4ab0d3287db9.marks:
Marking: First belief (1–2 marks) + Second belief (1–2 marks) + Source of authority named and applied (1–2 marks) = up to 6 marks.

Students may include some of the following points, but all other relevant points must be credited:
• Belief 1: Many Christians oppose the death penalty because it removes the possibility of repentance and reformation. Only God can take life that he created. The Bible teaches 'I take no pleasure in the death of the wicked, but rather that they turn from their ways and live' (Ezekiel 33:11). Jesus stopped a woman from being executed for adultery (John 8), showing people should be given the chance to reform.
• Belief 2: Islam's Shari'ah law permits the use of the death penalty as a deterrent. The Qur'an sets retaliation for murder (2:178). However, the next of kin can commute the sentence to imprisonment as an act of mercy upon payment of 'blood money'. 'If anyone is killed unjustly, we have granted the right of retribution to his heir' (Qur'an).

1 mark per simple point, 2 marks per developed point (maximum 4), plus 1 mark for relevant reference to scripture/sacred text.
[6 marks]

05a8055c-6c6b-4a22-9e43-4ab0d3287db9.text:
'The death penalty should never be used.'
Evaluate this statement.
In your answer you should:
• refer to religious arguments
• give reasoned arguments to support this statement
• give reasoned arguments to support a different point of view
• reach a justified conclusion.
05a8055c-6c6b-4a22-9e43-4ab0d3287db9.marks:
Arguments in support of the statement:
• Killing is wrong even if it involves killing a serious offender. It is against the sanctity of life and is 'playing God.'
• The most important aim of punishment is to reform. The death penalty does not allow time for repentance.
• It is neither loving nor compassionate. Jesus taught forgiveness, not retribution (John 8).
• 'I take no pleasure in the death of the wicked' (Ezekiel 33:11) / Ten Commandments – 'You shall not murder.'
• Legal systems can fail and innocent people can be killed. It contradicts the law on murder.
• Opposed by organisations such as the Muslim Peace Fellowship.
Arguments in support of other views:
• It acts as a deterrent and protects society.
• 'An eye for an eye' / 'Whoever sheds human blood, by humans shall their blood be shed' (Genesis 9:6).
• Shari'ah law allows for the death penalty for serious offences / hudud punishments.
• Some offenders cannot be reformed. It is the only way to totally protect society.
• It allows punishment to be downgraded as an act of mercy in Islam (blood money).
• The Principle of Utility – capital punishment protects society at large.
Top band (10-12): Well-argued, well-justified arguments for and against, linked together and leading to a reasonable conclusion with clear reference to religion.
Upper-mid band (7-9): Reasoned consideration of different points of view with clear reference to religion.
Lower-mid band (4-6): Reasoned consideration of a point of view with a logical chain of reasoning OR recognition of different points of view. Maximum lower-mid band if no reference to religion.
Low band (1-3): Point of view with reason(s) stated in support.
[12 marks]

05a8055c-6c6b-4a22-9e43-4ab0d3287db9.text: Explain two religious beliefs that show that the death penalty should not be supported. Refer to sacred writings or another source of religious belief and teaching in your answer.
05a8055c-6c6b-4a22-9e43-4ab0d3287db9.marks:
Marking: First belief (1–2 marks) + Second belief (1–2 marks) + Source of authority named and applied (1–2 marks) = up to 6 marks.

Students may include some of the following points, but all other relevant points must be credited:
• Belief 1: Christians believe only God has the right to take life because he created it. The sanctity of life means all human life is sacred. The Ten Commandments teach 'You shall not murder' (Exodus 20:13). Jesus taught forgiveness and stopped a woman being executed for adultery (John 8), showing reformation is more important than retribution.
• Belief 2: Many modern Muslims believe the death penalty is outdated, inhumane, and not applied fairly. The Muslim Peace Fellowship opposes it. The Qur'an teaches 'whoever saves a life, it will be as if they saved all of humanity' (Surah 5:32). Although Shari'ah law allows it, mercy through blood money is preferred.

1 mark per simple point, 2 marks per developed point (maximum 4), plus 1 mark for relevant reference to scripture/sacred text.
[6 marks]

91783d20-0104-44d2-bf13-57bbbd99fd0d.text:
Which of the following best describes God as omnipotent?
A) God is all-loving
B) God is all-powerful
C) God is all-knowing
D) God is everywhere
91783d20-0104-44d2-bf13-57bbbd99fd0d.marks: The correct answer is B. Omnipotent means all-powerful — God has unlimited authority and power. [1 mark]

91783d20-0104-44d2-bf13-57bbbd99fd0d.text: Name one of the three persons of the Trinity.
91783d20-0104-44d2-bf13-57bbbd99fd0d.marks: Any one from: the Father / the Son / the Holy Spirit. [1 mark]

91783d20-0104-44d2-bf13-57bbbd99fd0d.text: Explain two ways in which belief in God as loving (benevolent) influences Christians today.
91783d20-0104-44d2-bf13-57bbbd99fd0d.marks:
Students may include:
• Christians feel valued and loved by God, which gives them confidence and self-worth. They believe God cares about them individually, which brings comfort in difficult times.
• Christians are motivated to share God’s love with others through practical acts of kindness, charity work and forgiveness — imitating the unconditional love God shows them.
• Because God is all-loving, Christians believe in forgiveness. This influences them to forgive others who wrong them, just as God forgives those who repent.
• John 3:16 teaches that God loved the world enough to send Jesus. This influences Christians to make sacrifices for others.
Two clear, developed points needed for full marks. [4 marks]

91783d20-0104-44d2-bf13-57bbbd99fd0d.text: Explain two Christian beliefs about the nature of God. Refer to sacred writings or another source of Christian belief and teaching in your answer.
91783d20-0104-44d2-bf13-57bbbd99fd0d.marks:
Students may include:
• God is omnipotent — all-powerful. Supported by Luke 1:37: ‘Nothing is impossible with God.’ This was spoken by the Angel Gabriel to Mary, showing God’s power has no limits. (1–2 marks)
• God is benevolent — all-loving. Supported by John 3:16: ‘God so loved the world that he gave his one and only Son.’ Sending Jesus is seen as God’s greatest act of love. (1–2 marks)
• God is just — fair. Supported by 2 Thessalonians 1:6: ‘God is just: He will pay back trouble to those who trouble you.’ (1–2 marks)
• Source named and applied to the belief for additional marks.
Two beliefs, each explained and supported by a source of authority. [6 marks]

91783d20-0104-44d2-bf13-57bbbd99fd0d.text:
‘The problem of evil and suffering proves that God does not exist.’
Evaluate this statement considering arguments for and against. In your response you should:
• refer to Christian teachings
• reach a justified conclusion.
91783d20-0104-44d2-bf13-57bbbd99fd0d.marks:
Arguments supporting the statement:
• If God is all-powerful and all-loving, he would want to and be able to stop suffering — yet suffering exists.
• The inconsistent triad, an argument pressed by David Hume: God cannot be omnipotent, benevolent and allow evil to exist at the same time.
• Natural evil (earthquakes, disease) cannot be blamed on human free will, making it harder to explain.
Arguments against the statement:
• Moral evil is explained by free will — God gave humans genuine choice, and some misuse it. This is not God’s fault.
• Suffering may be a test of faith. The story of Job shows God rewards those who remain faithful through suffering.
• God’s plan is beyond human understanding — ‘Before I formed you in the womb I knew you’ (Jeremiah 1:5).
• Belief in God brings hope and comfort through suffering, especially the promise of eternal life.
Top band (10-12): both sides argued in depth, religious teaching used throughout, and a conclusion that follows from the reasoning.
Upper-mid band (7-9): both sides given with reasons and clear religious content.
Mid band (4-6): one side argued with reasons, or both sides stated without development. An answer with no religious content stays in this band at best.
Low band (1-3): an opinion with a reason.
[12 marks]

91783d20-0104-44d2-bf13-57bbbd99fd0d.text: Explain two ways in which the belief in the Trinity influences Christians today.
91783d20-0104-44d2-bf13-57bbbd99fd0d.marks:
Students may include:
• Christians are baptised ‘in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit’ (Matthew 28:19). This shows the Trinity is central to how Christians enter the faith and shapes their worship practices.
• Belief in the Holy Spirit gives Christians confidence that God is active in the world today — guiding, comforting and strengthening them in daily life and decision-making.
• The Trinity helps Christians understand God’s relationship with humanity: the Father as creator, the Son as saviour, and the Spirit as ongoing guide.
• Christians recite the Nicene Creed which affirms the Trinity, uniting believers across different denominations in a shared statement of faith.
Two clear, developed points needed for full marks. [4 marks]

008a76e3-5ab0-460d-a0ef-5f7c79074997.text: Give two examples of the ordinary Magisterium of the Catholic Church.
008a76e3-5ab0-460d-a0ef-5f7c79074997.marks: Award one mark for each correct example, up to two. Acceptable answers include: papal encyclical (e.g. Evangelium Vitae, Laudato Si') / the Catechism of the Catholic Church / a bishop's pastoral letter / an apostolic exhortation / the Bishops' Conference of England and Wales statement on a moral issue.

Top band: A large candle blessed and lit at the Easter Vigil, inscribed with the year, Alpha and Omega, and five grains of incense; it symbolises the risen Christ as the light of the world and is used at baptisms and funerals throughout the year.
Upper-mid band: A large candle lit at Easter, used at Catholic funerals and baptisms to symbolise the risen Christ.
Lower-mid band: A candle used at Catholic ceremonies.
Low band: A religious object used in church.

008a76e3-5ab0-460d-a0ef-5f7c79074997.text: Describe the significance of the Paschal Candle at a Catholic funeral.
008a76e3-5ab0-460d-a0ef-5f7c79074997.marks:
Top band: A detailed description covering: the Paschal Candle is first lit at the Easter Vigil to represent the risen Christ; its presence at a funeral connects the deceased to the paschal mystery (Christ's dying and rising); it symbolises the belief that the deceased has 'passed over' from death to life, just as Christ did; the same candle is used at baptism, linking the beginning and end of a Catholic's sacramental life; the symbols inscribed on it (Alpha and Omega, five wounds of Christ, the year) reinforce its theological meaning.
Upper-mid band: A clear description with at least two pieces of theological meaning.
Lower-mid band: Description of what the candle looks like without explaining its significance.
Low band: Vague reference to a candle at a funeral.

008a76e3-5ab0-460d-a0ef-5f7c79074997.text: Explain how the Second Vatican Council has influenced Catholic teaching on human dignity and the afterlife.
008a76e3-5ab0-460d-a0ef-5f7c79074997.marks:
Top band: A developed explanation covering: Vatican II (1962–65) produced Gaudium et Spes, which affirmed that death is the moment when the 'riddle of human existence' becomes most acute, and that the resurrection answers it; the council reformed the funeral rite to emphasise resurrection hope; Lumen Gentium re-centred the Church as 'the people of God' sharing in the paschal mystery; post-council encyclicals (Evangelium Vitae 65 on euthanasia, Salvifici Doloris on suffering) continued this development.
Upper-mid band: Two or more clear influences explained with reference to named documents.
Lower-mid band: One influence described without reference to specific documents.
Low band: Brief mention of Vatican II without substance.

008a76e3-5ab0-460d-a0ef-5f7c79074997.text:
Explain two Catholic beliefs about the role of the Magisterium as a source of authority.
Refer to a source of Catholic teaching in your answer.
008a76e3-5ab0-460d-a0ef-5f7c79074997.marks:
Top band: Two fully developed beliefs with sources. Belief 1 might be that the ordinary Magisterium (encyclicals, Catechism, bishops' pastoral letters) provides authoritative but non-infallible teaching on faith and morals, which Catholics are to adhere to with 'religious assent' (CCC 892). Belief 2 might be that the extraordinary Magisterium (ex cathedra pronouncements, ecumenical councils such as Vatican II) is infallible, guided by the Holy Spirit in fulfilment of Christ's promise to Peter (Matthew 16:18). Only two papal dogmas have been defined ex cathedra: the Immaculate Conception (1854) and the Assumption of Mary (1950).
Upper-mid band: Two beliefs explained with sources.
Lower-mid band: One belief well explained; the second superficial.
Low band: One brief point.

008a76e3-5ab0-460d-a0ef-5f7c79074997.text:
'Sacred art and music such as the Requiem are essential for Catholic funeral worship.'
Evaluate this statement.
In your answer you should:
• refer to Catholic teaching
• give reasoned arguments to support this statement
• give reasoned arguments to support a different point of view
• reach a justified conclusion.
008a76e3-5ab0-460d-a0ef-5f7c79074997.marks:
Arguments in support:
• Sacred music such as Fauré's Requiem (completed 1890) expresses the theology of resurrection hope in a way that spoken words cannot — the consoling, serene character of the In Paradisum and Lux Aeterna communicates confidence in God's mercy.
• The Paschal Candle, white pall, holy water and incense at Catholic funerals are theological statements as much as ritual actions: they proclaim resurrection faith through symbol.
• Vatican II's Sacrosanctum Concilium affirmed the importance of the arts in Catholic worship as a form of communication accessible to all believers regardless of education.
• Early Christian sarcophagi show that using art to express resurrection faith is as old as Christianity itself.

Arguments against:
• A minimalist or evangelical view might argue that heartfelt prayer and scripture are sufficient — elaborate ritual and art may distract from the essentials of faith.
• From a Humanist perspective, such rituals are comforting fictions that obscure the reality of death as the end of personal existence.
• Some Catholic communities in Britain opt for simple funeral Masses without elaborate music, arguing that prayerful simplicity is equally valid.

Conclusion: A justified conclusion should weigh the theological value of sacred art as a vehicle for doctrine against the argument that simpler forms of worship are equally effective.

Top band: Sophisticated argument with named sources and justified conclusion.
Upper-mid band: Both sides with some sources and a conclusion.
Lower-mid band: One-sided or conclusion missing.
Low band: Simple statements without reasoning.
